summary: Created an 8-phase plan (10h, 6 dependency waves). Phase 1 authors the reconciled draft-07 schema plus a new errors-format.md prose contract; Phases 2-3 build errors-append.sh with an append subcommand (direct events-append.sh port) then a novel update subcommand (read-modify-write held under one flock, validating the merged document before the atomic mv); Phase 4 adds a concurrency and off-schema-rejection regression suite; Phases 5-7 wire the deploy path, reconcile the three doc blocks, and convert the sole inline jq writer; Phase 8 bootstraps specs/errors.json and verifies end-to-end from the deployed tree.
decisions_made: Top level is object-with-array {"errors": [...]}, not a bare array: both live readers (orchestrator-postflight.sh, hooks/events-log-artifact.sh) already index .errors[] / .errors[-1], so this costs zero reader changes and admits a future schema_version key

errors-append.sh takes TWO subcommands (append, update), split across Phases 2 and 3 so append lands as an independent green milestone; update is original read-modify-write design with no precedent in core/scripts/ (events-append.sh is that directory's only flock user)
Validation is hand-written bash checks kept in sync with the schema doc, matching the events-append.sh idiom; no ajv or python3 -m jsonschema dependency is introduced

fix_status enum is unfixed|in_progress|fixed|resolved, with resolved documented as a DEPRECATED synonym for fixed so already-written cross-repo data validates on read; the update subcommand REJECTS resolved as an input value so the deprecation cannot re-propagate

recurrence_count is dropped from the persisted schema and /errors gains an explicit computed-at-query-time sentence; keeping an unwritten field would be a second dead-field defect of the kind this task exists to eliminate

The research report's Context Extension Recommendation was ACCEPTED: context/formats/errors-format.md is added alongside the schema, because the doc-block rewrites need a prose target for lazy-creation semantics, the CLI contract, the resolved deprecation, and the recurrence_count rationale, none of which a schema JSON can carry
id is schema-constrained as a non-empty string with a documented RECOMMENDED form err_{timestamp_ms}_{random6}, NOT an enforced pattern, so legacy err_001-style ids stay valid
context is the union superset (session_id, command, task, phase, checkpoint, agent, file) with NO individually required sub-fields, since no single writer populates them all
The subsumed source-store defect lane is added as a documented type value (source_store_defect), not as a new schema field
specs/errors.json is a specs/** runtime artifact authored directly with {"errors": []}, NOT a deploy artifact; errors-append.sh additionally lazily creates it in any repo
context/standards/error-handling.md's .agent-logs/errors.json block is explicitly OUT of scope: different path, different shape, no writer or reader anywhere
The UNBLOCKS 951/952/953 claim is recorded as advisory only, not a dependency edge; no work is planned for those tasks and completion is not gated on them
dead_ends: Do not plan a repo-wide sweep for inline '.errors +=' writers. Exactly one exists (skills/skill-planner/SKILL.md's jq Parse Failure recovery block); the other 18+ errors.json references in core are narrative prose with no executable jq. Phase 7 is sized as a one-file conversion with a confirming pre-edit grep
Do not introduce a runtime JSON-Schema-library call. jsonschema 4.26.0 is installed on this machine but is invoked nowhere in core/scripts/
Do not adopt the bare-array top-level form seen in the sibling repo's live specs/errors.json. It is the drift being corrected, not a precedent

Do not assume deploy-headless.sh will pick up the new script. The headless Load Core sync path does not always re-run copy_scripts for an already-loaded extension, so Phase 8 verifies .claude/scripts/errors-append.sh exists and is executable and applies the documented loader-primitive workaround if not. Never hand-author the file under .claude/** to work around this: it would be wiped by the next regeneration and would create a false green
